about: The o-story component map: which framework nouns each component owns, the story areas that test it, its neighbours, and the axis values that apply to it. o-story matrix derives the actions from a runtime's rows and operations and crosses them with these axes; o-story coverage compares the cells with the stories' covers. Validated by internal/storymatrix's tests.

key.why: a binding row: what a key does depends on everything around it, so a key action varies every axis its component has

keep.mode: a row answers only in its own modes
keep.placement: a key reaches a component through the stack walk, which a modal or the palette above it bounds
keep.focus: a page list without the focus is faded and its rows answer only once focused
keep.outcome: a key can succeed, meet a false guard, fail, land later, be cancelled or lose its owner
keep.data: motions, spills and cuts depend on how many rows there are and how wide they draw
keep.state: a filter, marks, a running job or restored state change what a key reaches
keep.size: a page's window, a table's columns and the hints change with the terminal size
keep.modifiers: a count, a register, dot-repeat, undo and macros change what a key runs

drop.to: a neighbour is where focus spills: the spill channel's
drop.direction: the direction of a spill: the spill channel's
drop.surface: footer or help is where hints show: the hints channel's

palette.why: the operation typed as a palette line: the line runs a request at the focus it opened over, so only its result varies

keep.outcome: the line can run, meet a false guard, fail, land later, be cancelled at a confirm or lose its owner

drop.direction: a palette line has no direction
drop.surface: a palette line is not a hint
drop.mode: the palette pins insert on its own line; the request runs whatever mode the key cells hold
drop.placement: the palette is always the modal on top; where the target sits is the key cells'
drop.focus: the request resolves its instance on the origin's focus path; focus is the key cells'
drop.data: the operation's handler gets the same request whatever the rows draw like; data is the key cells'
drop.state: the same request runs against the same state as a key; state is the key cells'
drop.size: the terminal size changes the palette's drawing (the palette component's own cells), not what the line runs
drop.modifiers: counts, registers, dot-repeat and macros are key prefixes; a line has none

cli.why: the operation as NOUN VERB on the command line: the CLI draws no screen, so only the result varies

keep.outcome: the call can succeed, meet a false guard, fail, settle a job, be refused at a confirm without --yes or lose its owner

drop.mode: a call carries its request, not a key: no mode answers it
drop.focus: a call names its --target; there is no focus to fade
drop.data: the CLI draws no rows; what a verb does with them is the key cells'
drop.state: a call runs against the state the key cells already vary
drop.modifiers: counts, registers, dot-repeat and macros are key prefixes; a call has none

parity.why: the same verb by key, palette line and CLI agree: a check across the channels, whose own cells vary the rest

keep.outcome: the three must agree on success and on each way of failing

drop.mode: the CLI and the palette have no key mode; the key cells vary it
drop.placement: the CLI draws no screen, so placement cannot be compared
drop.focus: the CLI names its target; focus cannot be compared
drop.data: the agreement is about the request, not the rows' drawing
drop.state: the three run against one state; each channel's own cells vary it

hosted.why: the component drawn in each placement: whether it fits its host

keep.placement: a page, a split panel, a modal and under the palette are different hosts with different bounds
keep.size: the host's bounds are cut from the terminal size; tiny and narrow terminals are where fitting breaks

drop.to: drawing in a host spills nowhere
drop.mode: the host is the same whatever mode answers; mode is the key cells'
drop.focus: the unfocused fade is drawn the same in every host; the key cells cross focus with every placement
drop.data: the key cells pair every data shape with every placement and size
drop.state: a filter or marks change the rows, not the host; the key cells pair state with placement

spill.why: the focus spilling into a neighbour: past a list's edge to the next or previous stop in drawing order

keep.to: each neighbour is a different stop to land on
keep.direction: past the last row goes to the next stop, before the first to the previous
keep.placement: a page stacks its stops top to bottom, a split puts them left before right (a modal clamps, so the code keeps page and split only)

drop.surface: a spill is not a hint
drop.mode: a spill is list.move, a normal-mode motion; its key cells carry the other modes
drop.focus: a spill starts from the focused stop by definition
drop.outcome: a spill lands or the list clamps, which the list.move key cells' outcomes hold
drop.data: a spill leaves from an edge whatever the rows; the list.move key cells vary data
drop.state: the list.move key cells vary state
drop.size: drawing order does not change with the terminal size
drop.modifiers: a counted move spills as one move; the list.move key cells vary counts

hints.why: the footer hints and ? help agree with the component's rows

keep.surface: the footer and ? help are built from the same rows with different rules (motions and hidden rows are off the footer)
keep.mode: the rows that answer, and so the hints, are per mode

drop.placement: a modal's hint line is the same BindingHints output for its focus; the rows differ by mode
drop.focus: hints are for the focused instance only
drop.data: the rows are the same whatever the data; a guarded row is the key cells' guard-false outcome
drop.state: a guarded row's state is the key cells' guard-false outcome
drop.size: the footer's cut by width is the chrome's one rule (Layout.Shell), not each component's

exclude.why: the palette holds the focus while it is open
insert belongs to the focused input: a focus change resets the mode
a visual selection is the focused stop's; leaving the stop resets the mode
the filter line is the focused list's; leaving it resets the mode
a pending mode is entered at the focus and cancelled by a focus change
a pending mode is entered at the focus and cancelled by a focus change
a pending mode is entered at the focus and cancelled by a focus change
the leader is pending on the focused terminal and cancelled by a focus change
passthrough is the focused terminal's pinned mode

components.title: Runtime core: app keys, modes, requests, inspection
Focus jumps: stops, regions, drawing order
Page lists: selection, motions, spills, marks
Tables: columns, cell mode, visual rows, yank, widths

keep.data: a table's column widths, cuts, wraps and drops are measured from its cells, so how it fits a host depends on the data

components.title: The list filter: / query, keep, choose, clear
Inputs and the editor (Readline and Vim tables)
Choosers (the page picker, column chooser, suggestions)
Declared settings and the Settings page
Bindings: ? help, bindings list, user bindings

exclude.why: J and K answer only under detail-scrolls, which needs the page's detail the verb then scrolls; the verb's one error (no detail on this page) cannot follow a key
an empty detail never overflows, so detail-scrolls is false and J and K do not answer
a one-line detail fits every window (at least one row), so detail-scrolls is false and J and K do not answer
J and K typed while the palette is open are its line's text; detail-scrolls is false under any modal
the pane divider is not a focus stop: no motion spills into it (the split it draws is the placement axis)

components.title: The jobs ticker and the jobs list
Chrome: pages, tabs, page picker, surface scroll, themes
Catalog data pages (groups rail, widgets, state deltas)
